rules.title: Berkeley prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Vendors may not sell, license, or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.key_value: Ban; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley, and vendors providing coordinated pricing algorithms to them.
rules.exemptions: Products publishing aggregated, anonymous data without recommending rents; products used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; market research for financing, appraisals, or software research/testing/training if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only if the landlord uses a coordinated pricing algorithm relying on nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.conflict_note: Official ordinance text shows amending Ord. 7,992-N.S. passed to print 2025-11-18 (second reading 2025-12-02) with no effective date; secondary sources give January 2026. Original Chapter 13.63 predates the amendment. RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice 2026-01-14.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions, including refusing to rent, terminating, or charging higher rent or deposit based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use banned; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Current and prospective tenants of rental housing in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner lives as primary residence; owner move-back agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner residence in 1-3 unit property; public housing/Section 8 status; owner move-back agreements; roommate/sublet situations.

rules.conflict_note: Source gives only the Council passage date (2020-04-14), not the effective date; treated as in force because the Rent Board administers complaints.

rules.title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 amounts, annually CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: Owners evicting for owner move-in must pay relocation assistance. Measure BB requires the Rent Board to adjust the amounts for inflation each year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley units covered by the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance evicted for owner move-in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when an owner move-in eviction occurs; qualifying-household criteria not stated.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (relocation provisions), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Effective date refers to the 2026 inflation adjustment approved by the Rent Board 2025-10-16, not the original enactment.

rules.title: Ellis Act withdrawal relocation assistance (2026 amounts)
rules.requirement: Owners evicting tenants to withdraw a property from the rental market must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Berkeley tenants evicted under an Ellis Act withdrawal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to Ellis Act withdrawal evictions; qualifying-household criteria not stated.

rules.conflict_note: Date refers to the 2026 inflation adjustment, not original enactment.

rules.title: Required Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement
rules.requirement: An owner charging an application or credit-report fee must give a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee and state the maximum fee permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of Berkeley residential property who charge screening or application fees.
rules.conflict_note: The statement's required URL is still to be provided by the City; no effective date stated.

rules.title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or adding/replacing a roommate; contrary lease terms are unenforceable.
rules.coverage_conditions: All Berkeley residential rental agreements, including existing leases.

rules.title: Berkeley rent ceilings and Annual General Adjustment (AGA), capped at 5% by Measure BB
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, landlords may raise rent ceilings only by the Rent Board's Annual General Adjustment (65% of Bay Area CPI change), capped at 5% under Measure BB (banked AGAs may exceed 5% to reach the ceiling). The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01, for eligible landlords who give required notice. Government-owned/subsidized units are now fully or partially covered.
rules.key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0%; AGA = 65% of CPI change, max 5%
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 (no rent control where Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 1980), single-family homes with tenancies beginning before 1996, rooming houses with 5+ individually rented rooms, and fully covered subsidized units (Section 8 vouchers, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME).
rules.exemptions: Partially covered (no rent ceiling): post-June-1980 new construction, single-family homes with tenancies from 1996-01-01, most condominiums, Section 202/811 units, and certain HUD-mortgaged project-based units. Fully exempt: Golden Duplex owner-occupied since 1979-12-31; shared kitchen/bath with owner resident at tenancy start; tenancies after 2018-11-07 on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives. 2026 AGA does not apply to tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family tenancy start date (before 1996); condominium status; Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, and ADU owner-occupancy exemptions; subsidy type and HUD mortgage status; Regulation 1148 eligibility and notice; Costa-Hawkins tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Rent Ordinance as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Sources describe the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as Certificate of Occupancy 'after June 1980'; the June 1980 CofO cutoff is used. Measure BB's effective date is not stated. Effective date shown is for the 2026 AGA. State AB 1482 cap yields to this stricter local rent control.

rules.title: Rent increase petitions only for completed capital improvements (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements; preliminary authorization for planned improvements is no longer available.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units subject to rent ceilings.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be fully covered by the Rent Ordinance.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

rules.title: Utility charges must be in base rent unless separately metered (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06 in fully covered units, utilities may be charged only as a set amount in base rent, or where separately metered and in the tenant's name per the lease. Adding utility costs to the ceiling requires a Rent Board petition.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units; tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06.
rules.exemptions: Separately metered utilities in the tenant's name as required by the lease.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start date on or after 2024-02-06; utility metering arrangement; unit fully covered.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: The 2024-02-06 applicability date predates the November 2024 election passing Measure BB; may be retroactive application or an error on the source page.

rules.title: Berkeley just cause required for evictions from fully or partially covered units
rules.requirement: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units: pre-1980 multifamily, single-family homes (any tenancy date), rooming houses, post-June-1980 new construction, most condominiums, subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex owner-occupied since 1979-12-31 and currently; shared kitchen/bath with an owner resident at tenancy start; tenancies after 2018-11-07 on owner-occupied ADU properties; university dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, ADU); ADU tenancy start date; dormitory or cooperative status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.conflict_note: No code citation or original enactment date in sources. State just cause (Civ. Code 1946.2) yields where this local ordinance applies.

rules.title: No nonpayment eviction for rental debt under one month's Fair Market Rent (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Eviction for nonpayment is allowed only if rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit in the Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR area.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

rules.title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

rules.title: Stricter requirements for lease-violation evictions (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Lease-breach evictions require a mutually agreed material term, actual harm to the landlord, and proof the tenant's behavior was unreasonable; notices must clearly describe the breach.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

rules.title: Eviction notice content and three-business-day filing with Rent Board
rules.requirement: Termination notices must reference Rent Board counseling; copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits (Berkeley Rent Ordinance)
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, prorated if the tenant moves out mid-year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex; shared kitchen/bath with resident owner; post-2018-11-07 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy exemptions; dormitory/cooperative status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.conflict_note: Interest rate and code section not given.

rules.title: Application screening fee capped at actual costs and $30 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable value of time, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted annually for CPI since 1998-01-01.
rules.key_value: Max $30/applicant CPI-adjusted; $68.96 for 2026 (per Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property charging applicants (including guarantors/cosigners) a screening fee.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt deposit/fee rules of federal or state housing assistance programs.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Housing-assistance program fee rules may govern instead.

rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) (as amended by Stats. 2025, ch. 67, AB 1170)
rules.conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170), but the $30 CPI-adjusted cap predates it; original effective date not in corpus. The $68.96 2026 figure comes from the Berkeley Rent Board.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when it knows or should have known that no unit is available now or within a reasonable time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property charging screening fees.
rules.conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); the provision existed earlier in some form, original date not in corpus.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-in-time process or full refund to non-selected applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a screening fee only if it offers either (A) a first-in-time process under written criteria approving the first qualified applicant and charging only when an application is considered, or (B) refunds to non-selected applicants within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission; 7-day refund for inadvertent concurrent fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property collecting screening fees.
rules.exemptions: No refund under the first-in-time option for applicants denied after consideration for failing screening criteria.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date taken from the AB 1170 amendment note; attribution of subdivision (c)(2) to that amendment is inferred.

rules.title: Itemized receipt and return of unused screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and return any portion not used for authorized screening.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents collecting an application screening fee.
rules.conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); original date not in corpus.

rules.title: Copy of credit report to fee-paying applicant within seven days
rules.requirement: If an applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must provide a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents collecting an application screening fee.
rules.conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); original date not in corpus.

rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent (AB 12)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent in addition to first month's rent, furnished or unfurnished. Small natural-person landlords may charge up to two months (separate rule).
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental security collected or demanded on or after 2024-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords under § 1950.5(c)(5) (natural person/family trust/all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total), except toward service members; advance payment of 6+ months' rent on a lease of 6+ months; agreed fees for tenant-requested alterations.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Small-landlord status depends on the owner's whole portfolio and ownership form; service member status; collection date.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date inferred from § 1950.5(c)(6) exempting security collected before 2024-07-01.

rules.title: Small landlord exception: security deposit up to two months' rent
rules.requirement: A natural-person landlord (incl. family trust or all-natural-person LLC) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total may collect security up to two months' rent; not available when the tenant is a service member.
rules.coverage_conditions: Qualifying small natural-person landlords.
rules.exemptions: Not available for service member tenants.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Four-unit / two-property limit applies across the owner's portfolio; ownership form; tenant service member status.

rules.conflict_note: Exception to the one-month cap; building max 4 units is necessary but not sufficient.

rules.title: Required move-out and move-in photographs for deposit deductions
rules.requirement: From 2025-04-01, landlords must photograph the unit after possession is returned, before and after repairs/cleaning to be deducted, and include photos with the itemized statement. For tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01, landlords must also photograph the unit at move-in.
rules.coverage_conditions: California residential tenancies with security deposits.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Move-in photo duty applies only to tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01.

rules.conflict_note: Move-out photos effective 2025-04-01; move-in photos for tenancies from 2025-07-01.

rules.title: Pre-move-out walk-through inspection must be offered
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of the tenancy so the tenant can address repairs or cleaning.
rules.coverage_conditions: California residential tenancies.
rules.citation: California security deposit statute (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5), as summarized by Berkeley Rent Board
rules.conflict_note: Source gives no subsection or effective date.

rules.title: Deposit return within 21 days with itemized statement; limits on deductions
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must return the deposit balance with an itemized statement and supporting receipts/invoices (unless deductions total $125 or less or validly waived). Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to move-in condition, and (if agreed) restoring personal property; professional cleaning only if reasonably necessary.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days; documentation required if deductions exceed $125
rules.coverage_conditions: All California residential tenancies where security was collected.
rules.exemptions: Documentation not required if deductions total $125 or less or tenant waived, unless requested within 14 days.

rules.title: Proof that deducted repairs were completed
rules.requirement: Starting 2025-01-01, landlords must provide proof that repairs charged against the deposit were completed.
rules.coverage_conditions: California residential tenancies with repair deductions.
rules.citation: California security deposit statute (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5), as summarized by Berkeley Rent Board
rules.conflict_note: Source gives no subsection citation.

rules.title: Service member higher security: written statement and return within six months
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member higher-than-standard security based on credit or housing history, it must give a written statement of amount and reason by lease signing and return the extra amount within six months.
rules.coverage_conditions: Service member tenants (Mil. & Vet. Code 400) renting a residence.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant is a service member charged higher security.

rules.title: No nonrefundable security
rules.requirement: A lease may not characterize any security as nonrefundable.
rules.coverage_conditions: All California residential rental agreements.

rules.title: Electronic return of deposit when paid electronically
rules.requirement: If security or rent was paid electronically, the remaining deposit must be returned electronically to a tenant-designated account unless otherwise agreed in writing; the landlord must notify the tenant of this right near the end of tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies where security or rent was paid electronically.
rules.exemptions: Prior written agreement designating another method.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether payments were made electronically.

rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(h)(1)(A)(ii), as amended by Stats. 2025, ch. 340 (AB 414)
rules.conflict_note: Attribution of this provision to the AB 414 amendment (effective 2026-01-01) is inferred.

rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service and emotional support animals
rules.requirement: Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for service or emotional support animals allowed as a disability accommodation.
rules.coverage_conditions: FEHA-covered housing providers.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant has a disability-related assistance animal.

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no section or effective date.

rules.title: Ban on higher security deposits based on protected characteristics
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not charge higher security deposits to households with children or applicants using Section 8 or other rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: FEHA-covered housing providers.
rules.exemptions: Qualifying senior housing as to age.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Senior housing qualification.

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no section or effective date.

rules.title: FEHA and Civil Rights Council limits on criminal history in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories; conviction-based denials must be directly related to tenancy suitability.
rules.key_value: No arrest-only, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records; no blanket bans
rules.coverage_conditions: Most California housing providers, including landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (discriminatory advertising still barred); certain shared-living, senior, and homeless youth housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person.

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act; Civil Rights Council (formerly FEHC) criminal history housing regulations
rules.conflict_note: 2020-01-01 is the regulations' effective date per a secondary trade-association source; no regulation section number given.

rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination ban including source of income (Section 8 / vouchers)
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass any person, including in screening (also by third-party screening companies), based on protected characteristics including source of income; since 2020-01-01 (SB 329) source of income includes housing subsidies such as Section 8, so 'No Section 8' policies and refusing subsidy paperwork are prohibited.
rules.key_value: Ban on refusing Section 8 / housing vouchers
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of any housing accommodation in California and those advertising rentals; tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (advertising still barred); shared-living single-sex preference; qualifying senior housing; some homeless youth housing. Inquiries into level or source of income are allowed.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy and senior housing exemptions.

rules.conflict_note: 2020-01-01 is when SB 329 extended source of income to housing subsidies; the underlying source-of-income protection is older. Last amended by SB 267 effective 2024-01-01.

rules.title: Credit history use for subsidized applicants requires alternative-evidence option (SB 267)
rules.requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, a housing provider may not use an applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent.
rules.key_value: Must offer alternative-evidence option before using credit history
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental applications involving a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, references, and identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applicant has a government rent subsidy.

rules.title: Income standard for subsidized tenants must use the tenant's portion of rent
rules.requirement: Where a government rent subsidy exists, a landlord may not use an income or financial standard not based on the portion of rent paid by the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental eligibility assessments involving a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, references, and identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applicant has a government rent subsidy.

rules.conflict_note: Original effective date not stated.

rules.title: Income standards must count aggregate income of co-residents
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use an income standard that fails to count the combined income of persons residing or proposing to reside together on the same basis as married persons.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental of housing accommodations in California.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade (AB 325)
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (used by two or more persons and using competitor data to recommend, set, or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade. Applies generally, including rental pricing.
rules.key_value: Prohibition; criminal fines up to greater of $6M or 2x gain/loss (corporations), civil fines up to $1M per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer, including landlords and rental software providers.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement restraining trade.

rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.conflict_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06; 2026-01-01 effective date inferred from California's default rule and confirmed by secondary source. General antitrust law, not housing-specific; operates alongside local bans.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on coercing adoption of common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325)
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm while coercing another to adopt a price or commercial term it recommends for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on coercing adoption of algorithm-recommended prices or terms
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer using or distributing a common pricing algorithm.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion to adopt algorithm recommendations.

rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.conflict_note: Effective date inferred from default rule; what constitutes coercion is left to courts.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction requirement (Civ. Code 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied for 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance equal to one month's rent (payment within 15 days or waiver of final month's rent).
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome park units, after 12/24 months of occupancy, where no qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to two units/bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU); certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate-member LLC with required exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners; properties under a qualifying local just cause ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Occupancy duration; for separately alienable units, owner entity type and exemption notice; owner occupancy; deed-restricted affordable housing; whether a local just cause ordinance applies.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date is the operative date of the current text; original AB 1482 protections date to 2020. Last amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01; repealed 2030-01-01. Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before 2019-09-01 or more protective later ordinances.

rules.title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code 1947.12)
rules.requirement: Over any 12-month period, gross rent may not rise more than 5% plus regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months; at most two increases per 12 months.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property (incl. mobilehome park units) not subject to stricter local rent control and not exempt.
rules.exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; stricter local rent control; separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate-member LLC with written exemption notice; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU) where owner lived there at tenancy start; mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner entity type and exemption notice for separately alienable units; owner-occupied duplex; affordable-housing restrictions; dormitory status; whether stricter local rent control applies.

rules.conflict_note: Applies to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (mobilehomes 2021-02-18); current text re-added by SB 567, operative 2024-04-01; repealed 2030-01-01. Yields where stricter local rent control applies.

rules.title: Temporary relocation payments for capital improvement displacement under 20 days (San Francisco)
rules.requirement: Relocation for temporary capital improvement displacements in San Francisco lasting less than 20 days is governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 rather than SF Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
rules.key_value: $446/day plus actual moving expenses (3/1/26-2/28/27, per SF Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Temporary capital improvement evictions in San Francisco lasting less than 20 days.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days.

rules.conflict_note: The daily amount is from the SF Rent Board current-rates page (c175).

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: criminal history limits
rules.requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket bans and must assess applicants individually; they may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged records, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old.
rules.key_value: Convictions older than 5 years may not be considered
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units.
rules.exemptions: Direct relationship to the housing sought or unreasonable safety risk; current criminal behavior; conflicting federal/state requirements preempt.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

rules.citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.conflict_note: Administrative policy applied through funding/IDP agreements, not a general ordinance; current status not confirmed.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: credit score and history limits
rules.requirement: Covered providers may not use credit scores to approve or deny; credit history may be used only in lieu of unavailable rental history, and lack of credit history is not grounds for rejection.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or BPDA IDP income-restricted units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

rules.citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.conflict_note: Administrative policy; current status not confirmed.

rules.title: Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd session) - not enacted
rules.requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement rent stabilization; sent to a study order (H5035) 2024-09-09 and died at session end. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Boston residential rental housing (proposed).
rules.conflict_note: Local rent control remains barred by M.G.L. c. 40P absent state enactment.

rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744) - not enacted
rules.requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement tenant eviction protections; sent to a study order 2024-09-09 and not enacted. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Boston residential tenants (proposed).
rules.conflict_note: 193rd session ended without enactment.

rules.title: Boston fair housing ban including rental assistance discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on protected classes including rental assistance (e.g., Section 8), family status, and military status.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any housing rented, sold, or financed in Boston.
rules.citation: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission (section not stated)
rules.conflict_note: Summary page; no ordinance citation, effective date, or exemptions; commission also enforces state/federal law.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the notice to quit or non-renewal, and file a copy with the City.
rules.key_value: Notice with every notice to quit/non-renewal; $300/day for 2nd+ offense
rules.coverage_conditions: All Boston landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy.
rules.exemptions: Hospitals, skilled nursing/health facilities, nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when a tenancy is being terminated or not renewed.

rules.citation: City of Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Oct. 2020); penalties Sec. 10-11.7
rules.conflict_note: Notice requirement only; not a just-cause standard and violations do not halt eviction. Categorized as closest fit.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance incl. source of income
rules.requirement: Landlords and agents may not discriminate in viewing, renting, or tenancy terms based on protected categories including source of income; reasonable standards applied uniformly are allowed.
rules.key_value: Source of income (Section 8, public benefits) protected
rules.coverage_conditions: Cambridge rental housing transactions.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied 2-family dwellings.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of 2-family dwelling.

rules.conflict_note: Summary page; no effective date.

rules.title: Cambridge policy order to develop a ban on algorithmic rent-pricing software
rules.requirement: City Council directed the city manager to draft options to bar residential property managers from contracting with algorithmic/AI rent-recommendation companies. No ordinance enacted.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential property management companies in Cambridge (proposed).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Scope not yet drafted.

rules.citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (number not given)
rules.conflict_note: Policy order only; date not stated.

rules.title: H.5222: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing (pending)
rules.requirement: Pending bill that would restrict algorithmic rent fixing; reported favorably 2026-03-12 as a new draft of H1564 and referred to House Ways and Means. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts rental housing market (proposed).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text not in corpus.

rules.conflict_note: Substantive terms unknown.

rules.title: S.2983: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (pending)
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill (new draft of S.994 and S.1016) that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting; reported 2026-03-12 and referred to Senate Ways and Means. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential rental housing (proposed).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text not in corpus.

rules.conflict_note: No further action shown as of 2026-10-01.

rules.title: Housing discrimination and prohibited applicant inquiries (publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, contiguously located housing)
rules.requirement: Owners, brokers, and agents may not refuse to rent or discriminate based on protected characteristics, and may not make inquiries or records about those characteristics of applicants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, or contiguously located housing as defined in c.151B § 1.
rules.exemptions: Age protection does not apply to minors or qualifying elderly housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Housing-type definitions in c.151B § 1 not in corpus.

rules.title: Housing discrimination and prohibited inquiries (other covered housing)
rules.requirement: Owners and agents of other covered housing may not discriminate or make inquiries on protected bases including veteran status and handicap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Other covered housing accommodations under c.151B § 1.
rules.exemptions: Leasing a single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; age exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of two-family dwelling.

rules.title: Ban on discrimination against public assistance and housing subsidy recipients
rules.requirement: Anyone furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies (e.g., vouchers) or because of program requirements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person furnishing rental accommodations in Massachusetts.

rules.title: Ban on refusing to rent to households with children
rules.requirement: Owners and agents may not refuse to rent or discriminate because children will occupy the unit; occupancy limits still apply.
rules.coverage_conditions: Publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, contiguously located, or other covered housing.
rules.exemptions: Dwellings of three or fewer units with an elderly (65+) or infirm occupant; temporary leasing (up to one year) of owner's principal residence; one unit of an owner-occupied two-family dwelling.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; elderly/infirm occupant; temporary owner absence.

rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease; right to cure
rules.requirement: To end a written lease for nonpayment, the landlord must give 14 days' written notice; the tenancy continues if the tenant pays all rent due with interest and costs by the answer date.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice; cure by answer date
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies under a written lease with unpaid rent.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Written lease; unpaid rent.

rules.conflict_note: Procedural nonpayment rule, not a just-cause requirement; Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause law in corpus.

rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: At or before tenancy start, a landlord may collect only first and last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent (properly held, with statement of condition), and lock/key cost.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential tenancies.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less excluded.

rules.conflict_note: St. 2025, c. 9 (effective 2025-08-01) extended clause (b) to lessor's agents; the cap predates it.

rules.title: Ban on application fees and other up-front charges by lessor or lessor's agent
rules.requirement: Neither a landlord nor its agent may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay anything beyond first and last month's rent, a security deposit, and lock/key cost at or before tenancy start; application, pet, cleaning and similar fees are barred.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, deposit, and lock fee; application fees prohibited
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential tenancies; lessors and (since 2025-08-01) their agents.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less; licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 CMR 7.00 subject to M.G.L. c. 112 § 87DDD1/2.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether a fee is charged by a licensed broker; vacation rentals.

rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9
rules.conflict_note: Statute does not expressly name application fees; secondary source says the bar has been in effect since the 1970s. Extension to agents effective 2025-08-01. Third-party screening-service charges are unsettled.

rules.title: Optional fee in lieu of security deposit, capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: EOHLC may authorize an optional fee in lieu of a security deposit, offered to all approved applicants, totaling (with any deposit) no more than one month's rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Where lessor offers a fee in lieu under EOHLC regulations.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Operative only to the extent EOHLC has issued regulations and lessor elects.

rules.conflict_note: Corpus does not state whether regulations have been issued.

rules.title: Deposit held in separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account
rules.requirement: Deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account beyond creditors' reach; tenant receipt with bank, amount, and account number within 30 days.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential lessors holding deposits.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.title: Statement of condition required with security deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord accepting a deposit must give a signed statement of the unit's condition upon receipt or within 10 days after tenancy starts, whichever is later; tenant has 15 days to add damage.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential lessors accepting deposits.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: A landlord holding a deposit one year or longer must pay yearly interest from the first day of tenancy at 5% or the lesser bank rate, with an annual statement; tenant may deduct unpaid interest from rent.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser bank rate
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential lessors holding deposits 1+ year.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.title: Receipt and interest on prepaid last month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord collecting last month's rent in advance must give a receipt and pay yearly interest at 5% or the lesser bank rate from the first day of tenancy.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser bank rate
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts lessors collecting last month's rent in advance.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days; limited deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit or balance within 30 days after tenancy ends; deductions only for unpaid rent/water, tax-escalation increases, and damage beyond wear and tear with sworn itemized list and evidence.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential lessors holding deposits.
rules.exemptions: Vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor owner
rules.requirement: On transfer of the property, the deposit and interest must pass to the successor, who must notify the tenant within 45 days and is liable for return.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential property transfers where a deposit is held.
rules.exemptions: Municipalities acquiring under c. 60; foreclosing chartered financial institution mortgagees (as to successor liability); vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Ownership transfer and successor type.

rules.conflict_note: Successor-type exemptions relate to acquirer status, not landlord size.

rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection and six-month reprisal presumption
rules.requirement: Landlords may not retaliate against tenants for protected activity; a termination notice (except for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial change within six months of protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal.
rules.key_value: 6-month presumption; damages 1-3 months' rent or actual damages
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential tenants engaging in protected activity.
rules.exemptions: Termination notices for nonpayment of rent excluded from presumption.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Protected activity within prior six months.

rules.conflict_note: Anti-retaliation statute, not a general just-cause requirement.

rules.title: Licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees only with written disclosure
rules.requirement: Only licensed brokers/salespersons may charge prospective tenants a housing-finding fee, with signed written notice at first meeting of amount, timing, and whether contingent on a lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: Licensed real estate brokers and salespersons.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Broker licensure and notice given.

rules.conflict_note: Since 2025-08-01, M.G.L. c. 112 § 87DDD1/2 limits payment of broker fees to the party that engaged the broker.

rules.title: Rental broker fee paid only by the party that hired the broker
rules.requirement: Any broker fee may only be paid by the party (lessor or tenant) who engaged and contracted with the broker; tenants cannot be charged for a landlord-hired broker.
rules.key_value: Fee paid only by engaging party
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential rentals involving a licensed broker.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Which party engaged the broker.

rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43)
rules.conflict_note: Broker-fee rule placed under application_screening_fees as closest category.

rules.title: Required tenant-rights form with notice to quit for nonpayment
rules.requirement: A notice to quit for nonpayment must include the state form on repayment, rental assistance, court rules, and eviction restrictions; courts may not accept nonpayment eviction filings without proof of delivery.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential notices to quit for nonpayment in Massachusetts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Nonpayment notices only.

rules.conflict_note: Procedural notice rule, categorized as closest fit.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 statewide rent cap - struck from November 2026 ballot (not law)
rules.requirement: Would have repealed M.G.L. c. 40P and capped annual rent increases for most units at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC (Cella v. Attorney General) barred it from the November 2026 ballot because of its religious exemption. No state rent cap is in force.
rules.key_value: Proposed: lesser of CPI or 5% (never effective)
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units statewide (proposed).
rules.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units; units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; educational, religious, or nonprofit facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, institutional facilities.

rules.citation: Mass. Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (June 23, 2026)
rules.conflict_note: Ruling date reported as June 23, 2026 (one sidebar says June 24). Legislative compromise bill was not passed; proponents may pursue 2028. M.G.L. c. 40P still bars local rent control.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services (e.g., RealPage-type revenue management software using nonpublic competitor data) to set rents; public and private enforcement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City.
rules.exemptions: Per news report, real estate agents excluded; other exclusions unclear.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the landlord uses an algorithmic rent coordination service.

rules.conflict_note: Secondary sources only; effective date given only as June 2025. NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43), effective 2027-07-01, § 6(b) bars municipal ordinances conflicting with the Act, so this ordinance may be preempted in part once the Act takes effect.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
rules.requirement: Rent increases on covered properties are regulated (CPI-based); increases above the allowed amount require landlord applications (capital improvement, vacancy capital improvement, hardship).
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties with 5 or more units in Jersey City unless exempt.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties; other ordinance exemptions via Rent Control Exemption Request; newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt for 30 years under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Other exemptions via approved Rent Control Exemption Request; 'newly constructed' status under state law measured from completion of construction.

rules.conflict_note: Allowable increase formula not stated in corpus. 30-year exemption derived from state statute N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on software/algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Hoboken.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where such software or platforms are used.

rules.conflict_note: Secondary source; citation may be Chapter 158, Article II; effective date given only as July 2025. NJ FAIR Act § 6(b) (effective 2027-07-01) bars conflicting municipal ordinances.

rules.title: FAIR Act (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent), P.L.2026, c.43
rules.requirement: Rental property owners and agents may not pay for or use a coordinator (algorithmic revenue management software/device using competitors' nonpublic, competitively sensitive data to set or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy). No person may perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent coordination using nonpublic competitor data
rules.coverage_conditions: All owners of residential rental units in New Jersey and their agents, and coordinators/software providers.
rules.exemptions: Inpatient medical, licensed long-term care, and correctional facilities; research/statistical uses not used to set prices; free public rent estimates; equal-terms listing databases; government affordability controls; non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where coordinating algorithmic software/devices are used.

rules.conflict_note: Approved 2026-07-20; effective first day of the twelfth month after enactment = 2027-07-01, so not yet effective on 2026-10-01. § 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances, potentially preempting parts of Jersey City and Hoboken bans once effective.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: no criminal history inquiry before conditional offer
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about criminal records before a conditional offer, except methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act (seventh month after 2021-06-18 enactment).

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: written criminal-screening disclosure before accepting application fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, providers must disclose in writing whether criminal history is reviewed and that applicants may submit evidence of inaccuracy, rehabilitation, or mitigating factors.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: records that can never be considered
rules.requirement: Providers may never evaluate applicants on arrests/charges without conviction, expunged, pardoned, or vacated convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: conviction lookback periods and individualized assessment
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, providers may consider only listed serious convictions and recent indictable convictions within lookback windows; withdrawing an offer requires an individualized assessment and a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest shown by preponderance of evidence.
rules.key_value: 1st degree: 6 yrs; 2nd/3rd: 4 yrs; 4th: 1 yr; murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, lifetime sex offender registry: any time
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: ban on ads excluding people with criminal records
rules.requirement: Providers may not publish ads or use applications stating applicants with arrests or convictions will not be considered (except meth/sex-offender exceptions), nor misuse applicants' records.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: ban on drug or alcohol testing of applicants
rules.requirement: Providers may not require drug or alcohol tests or seek consent to obtain drug treatment facility information.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey housing providers of rental dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building of four or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the act.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50 (CPI-adjusted from 2027)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee exceeding $50 to lease or sublease a residential unit; CPI-adjusted annually starting 2027-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property except units in one- or two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: One- and two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless they are the landlord.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Licensee exemption when a real estate licensee (not the landlord) charges the fee.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed: first day of fourth month after 2026-01-20 approval. An older DCA guide stating no specific state fee cap predates this law.

rules.title: Security deposit capped at 1.5 months' rent; annual increases capped at 10%
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a deposit above 1.5 times monthly rent; yearly deposit increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid last month's rent and pet deposits count toward the cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most New Jersey residential rentals, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant requests compliance in writing (effective 30 days later).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; tenant written opt-in.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days with itemized deductions
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after tenancy ends, the landlord must return deposit plus interest less itemized deductions sent by personal delivery or registered/certified mail; double damages for wrongful withholding.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies under the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless tenant opts in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; tenant opt-in; lease-break timing.

rules.title: Deposit held in trust in interest-bearing NJ account; interest belongs to tenant
rules.requirement: Deposits must be held in trust in an insured NJ interest-bearing account or qualifying money market fund, with written notice within 30 days and annually; interest belongs to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: New Jersey landlords holding security deposits (investment options differ for 10+ units).
rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals of 125 consecutive days or less; owner-occupied 2-3 family dwellings unless tenant opts in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Seasonal rental; owner occupancy; tenant opt-in.

rules.title: Deposit return within 5 business days after displacement
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit within five business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation with official posting or certification of 7+ days.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Official displacement notice or certification.

rules.title: Deposit return within 15 business days after domestic-violence lease termination
rules.requirement: After a Safe Housing Act termination, the landlord must make the deposit plus interest available within 15 business days and notify the tenant within 3 business days of pickup details.
rules.coverage_conditions: Domestic violence victims terminating under the Safe Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: Transient or seasonal rentals.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: DV lease termination with documentation.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)-(r)); notice requirements apply.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most NJ residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming/boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or three units and no more than two rental units; transient/seasonal hotel guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of 2-3 unit buildings; transient/seasonal status.

rules.title: Six months' rent relocation for illegal-occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted to correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance of six times monthly rent paid by the landlord; unpaid amounts accrue 18% interest and become a lien.
rules.coverage_conditions: Evictions on the illegal occupancy ground.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Eviction must be for illegal occupancy.

rules.conflict_note: Source cites both 2A:18-61.1(g) and (h).

rules.title: Owner move-in eviction requires six months of personal occupancy
rules.requirement: After evicting for personal occupancy, the landlord must occupy the unit at least six months; otherwise treble damages plus fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units vacated after owner personal-occupancy notice.

rules.title: Rent increases may not be unconscionable; no mid-lease increases
rules.requirement: Landlords may not raise rent mid-lease and must use proper notices; tenants cannot be evicted for nonpayment of an unconscionable increase or one violating municipal rent control. No numeric state cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Same as the Anti-Eviction Act (e.g., owner-occupied 2-3 unit premises).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unconscionability is fact-specific and court-determined.

rules.conflict_note: NJ has no state rent control law; municipal ordinances apply in addition.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings within 30 years after completion.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies to buildings within 30 years of construction completion that qualify as 'newly constructed' under the statute.

rules.conflict_note: State preemption of local rent control for new buildings, overriding municipal ordinances such as Jersey City's.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover condominium/cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: Rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in buildings undergoing conversion.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Building undergoing conversion.

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: protected classes including source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate based on protected classes, including source of lawful income or rent payment (e.g., Section 8 vouchers).
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental of real property in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: One unit of an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner/occupant's one-family home; religious organization preferences; single-sex residences; older-persons housing as to familial status.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; religious organization; older-persons housing.

rules.conflict_note: DCR brochure is a 2015 revision; later source-of-income amendments not reflected.

rules.title: San Diego prohibition on sale and use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use an algorithmic device (software analyzing nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy) to set rents or occupancy for San Diego residential property, and no person may sell, license, or provide such a device to a landlord.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property a separate violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in San Diego (SDMC § 98.0702) and vendors.
rules.exemptions: Reports from aggregated nonpublic data more than 90 days old or public data that do not recommend future rents; software used for affordable housing program rents/income limits.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where software uses nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy.

rules.conflict_note: Official materials are the Feb. 2025 draft ordinance (passage date blank; effective 30 days after passage). Secondary sources report the ban in effect from June 2025 and litigated in Keller v. UDR (S.D. Cal.); status in_force based on those.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections Ordinance: just cause required
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause; curable violations require notice to cure; owner move-in for leases from 2023-06-24 requires tenant agreement or lease clause; substantial-remodel terminations require permits and notices.
rules.key_value: Just cause required for tenancies over 30 days
rules.coverage_conditions: San Diego residential rental property incl. mobilehome units; tenancies over 30 days, excluding fixed-term leases of 3 months or less.
rules.exemptions: Hotels/short-term rentals; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); MRL mobilehomes; care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family homes (up to 2 rented units/bedrooms); owner-occupied duplexes; certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable units of non-corporate owners with exemption notice.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner entity type and exemption notice; owner occupancy; shared facilities; affordable housing restrictions; tenancy length.

rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0701-98.0710 (O-21647 N.S., amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.conflict_note: Amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28. Supplements Civ. Code 1946.2, which yields to qualifying local ordinances.

rules.title: San Diego no-fault termination relocation assistance and right of first refusal
rules.requirement: For no-fault terminations, the landlord must pay two months' actual rent (three for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants) as direct payment within 15 days or rent waiver, give required notice, and honor the tenant's re-rental right.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+ or disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Covered San Diego tenancies terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of income or tenancy length.
rules.exemptions: Same as § 98.0703; none where a government agency/court finds the tenant at fault for a vacate order.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: No-fault ground; tenant age/disability; ordinance exemptions.

rules.conflict_note: Credited against relocation owed under other laws. Commission notice requirement applies 30 days after its portal is established; status as of 2026-10-01 unverified.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy
rules.requirement: Selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to set rents or manage occupancy for San Francisco residential units is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month per affected unit may be separate
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; sellers and landlord users of qualifying devices.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether the device uses nonpublic competitor rental data.

rules.conflict_note: Board approved July 2024; official page gives 2024-10-14. Now at issue in Gomez v. Greystar (N.D. Cal.).

rules.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance: criminal history in affordable housing
rules.requirement: Protects applicants and residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions; specific limits not described in corpus.
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to affordable housing; qualifying properties not defined in corpus.

rules.conflict_note: Summary page only; no code citation or effective date.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: Evicting a tenant from a Rent Ordinance unit requires one of 17 enumerated just causes that is the dominant motive; lease expiration or ownership change is not just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions, including some units exempt from rent limits (e.g., post-1979-06-13 new construction, Costa-Hawkins tenancies).
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance (not listed in corpus).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit coverage under eviction provisions; government-regulated tenancies vary.

rules.conflict_note: State just cause yields where this local ordinance applies.

rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase from 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28 is 1.6% of base rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units first obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy after 1979-06-13 and Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies are exempt from rent increase limits (per Rent Board just cause overview).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins exemptions (e.g., single-family homes/condos) and government-regulated tenancies.

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37); Rent Board annual allowable increase
rules.conflict_note: Rate expires 2027-02-28; prior 1.4% (2025-26). CofO cutoff taken from c167. State AB 1482 yields to this local rent control.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate (2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28)
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate, 4.2% for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: San Francisco residential security deposits.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board Security Deposit Interest Rates (Form 572)
rules.conflict_note: No ordinance section given; prior 5.0% (2025-26).

rules.title: Relocation payments for owner/relative move-in, demolition/removal, capital improvement, and substantial rehabilitation evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting on these grounds must pay relocation; for notices served 3/1/26-2/28/27: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly (60+)/disabled tenant or household with minor children.
rules.coverage_conditions: San Francisco Rent Ordinance tenancies terminated on the listed no-fault grounds.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions under 20 days governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Eviction ground, notice service date, and tenant age/disability/children.

rules.conflict_note: Amounts indexed annually; effective date reflects current rate period.

rules.title: Relocation payments for Ellis Act evictions
rules.requirement: For Ellis Act eviction notices served 3/1/26-2/28/27: $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: San Francisco tenants evicted under the Ellis Act.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Ellis Act withdrawal; notice date; tenant age/disability.

rules.conflict_note: Amounts indexed annually.

rules.title: Santa Ana Ordinance NS-3090 ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision, and use of algorithmic rent-setting software using nonpublic competitor data for Santa Ana residential property; tenants need only prove use, not collusion.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords and software vendors in Santa Ana.
rules.exemptions: Software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data; tools used for affordable housing program compliance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where software relies on nonpublic competitor data.

rules.conflict_note: First reading 2026-02-17, final adoption early March 2026 (reported pending in one source); effective 2026-04-02 per Morgan Lewis. Municipal code section not given. Landlord association suggested interaction with state law (AB 325); no preemption established.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Rent may be raised once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change (0% if CPI negative); the City publishes the rate by June 30, effective September 1.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential buildings constructed on or before 1995-02-01 and mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before 1990-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after 1995-02-01; mobile home spaces offered after 1990-01-01; fair-return petitions may allow more.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Mobile home space dates; fair-return petitions; Costa-Hawkins exemptions not stated in corpus.

rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.conflict_note: No municipal code citation in corpus. State AB 1482 yields to this stricter local cap.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of occupancy, an owner may terminate only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause after notice and opportunity to cure; no-fault terminations require three months' relocation assistance or rent waiver.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 30 days; 3 months relocation for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Santa Ana residential tenancies after 30 days of occupancy.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotels/transient; care facilities; dormitories; shared living quarters.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy over 30 days; affordable, transient, care-facility, dormitory, shared-living exemptions.

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (2021)
rules.conflict_note: Source does not say whether the 15-year cutoff is measured by construction or certificate of occupancy; no code citation.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords of non-RSO units may not terminate tenancies without a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most City of Los Angeles rentals not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than 1978-10-01 and single-family dwellings, once the tenant has lived there 6 months or the original lease expired.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some nonprofit homeless or substance-abuse facilities, some HACLA/government properties; RSO units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit not regulated by RSO (generally built after 1978-10-01, or single-family dwellings of any age); tenancy of 6+ months or lease expired; excluded facility types.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance, LAMC § 165.01 et seq. (cited § 165.05)
rules.conflict_note: No effective date in corpus. Year cutoff not used as a strict filter because pre-1978 single-family dwellings fall under JCO.

rules.title: Nonpayment eviction limited to arrears exceeding Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO and JCO units may not evict for nonpayment unless the tenant owes more than one month's Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Arrears must exceed one month's FMR
rules.coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO units in Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit covered by RSO or JCO.

rules.citation: Los Angeles renter protections (LAMC section not stated)

rules.title: Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices to RSO and JCO tenants must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service; for no-fault evictions, the notice may be served only after filing the Declaration of Intent to Evict.
rules.key_value: File within 3 business days of service
rules.coverage_conditions: All JCO and RSO units in Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit covered by RSO or JCO.

rules.citation: Los Angeles RSO/JCO (LAMC Ch. XV, Art. 1 and Art. 5)
rules.conflict_note: Relocation Bulletin A says 3 days; Bulletin B and LAHD page say 3 business days.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised once every 12 months by the LAHD-published allowable percentage; rent may reset to market after voluntary vacancy, buyout, or specified at-fault eviction. Registered RSO/SCEP fee pass-throughs allowed with notice.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months by LAHD allowable %; 3% applied 7/1/2025-6/30/2026
rules.coverage_conditions: City of Los Angeles rental properties first built on or before 1978-10-01 (apartments, condos, duplexes, two or more SFDs on a parcel, etc.), plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28.
rules.exemptions: Condo/townhome tenancies beginning after 1995-12-31 (rent not regulated); luxury exemption based on May 1978 rent; temporary exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Replacement units covered regardless of age; condo/townhome tenancy date; luxury exemption; single SFD on a parcel not covered.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, LAMC Ch. XV
rules.conflict_note: LAHD calculator retrieved 2026-10-01 still shows 3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026, a period that has ended; the 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 percentage is not in the corpus and the formula changed (utility and dependent add-ons eliminated 2026-02-02). Source says 'first built', ordinance may key on certificate of occupancy. State AB 1482 yields to RSO.

rules.title: LA RSO: no additional percentage increase for utilities
rules.requirement: Since 2026-02-02, RSO landlords may not add any extra percentage increase for utilities on top of the annual allowable increase.
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit subject to RSO.
